title: 2D dynamic programming
short: Fill a grid of answers, each cell built from its neighbors.
what: When an answer depends on two things, like a row and a column, or a spot in each of two words, the saved answers form a table. Fill it row by row. Each cell is built from cells you already filled: usually the one above, the one to the left, or the one diagonally up-left.
analogy: Counting routes through city blocks to a friend's house. The routes to any corner are the routes to the corner above plus the routes to the corner on the left.

frames.label: ways to reach each cell
frames.say: A robot starts top-left and can only move right or down. How many different routes reach the bottom-right of a 3 x 4 grid?

frames.label: ways to reach each cell
frames.say: There is only one way to reach each cell in the top row: keep going right. Same for the left column: keep going down.

frames.label: ways to reach each cell
frames.say: You can enter a cell only from above or from the left. So ways = above + left. For row 1, c1: 1 + 1 = 2.

frames.label: ways to reach each cell
frames.say: Keep going left to right: 1 + 2 = 3, then 1 + 3 = 4. Each cell needs only cells that are already filled.

frames.label: ways to reach each cell
frames.say: The last cell: 4 + 6 = 10 routes. 12 cells, each filled once with one addition, instead of tracing every route.

when: Compare two strings (common part, edit distance)
The state needs two numbers, like i and j
cost: Fill an m x n table
watch: Build the table with a loop: [[0] * cols for _ in range(rows)]. [[0] * cols] * rows shares one row.
Fill the first row and column first; they have no cell above or to the left.
For two strings, add an extra row and column for the empty string.
